title: Qcqs derived pushforward preserves coproducts with a common lower bound
statement: Fix universes u and u+1. Let $\Lambda$ be any commutative condensed ring with specified multiplication, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of schemes in universe u [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]. Put $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ and $D_T=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T})$ for $T=X,Y$, using ordinary module sheaves and ordinary unbounded derived categories [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Let I be any type in universe u+1, let N be an integer, and let $K_i\in D_X$ for i in I satisfy $H^n(K_i)=0$ whenever n<N [def-kun-truncations]. Then the actual total derived pushforward $Rf_*:D_X\to D_Y$ preserves the colimit of this I-indexed discrete diagram. Equivalently, the canonical coproduct comparison $\bigoplus_i Rf_*K_i\to Rf_*(\bigoplus_iK_i)$ is an isomorphism. I may be empty. No adic, constructibility, properness, finite-type, or common upper-bound assumption is required.

proof.text: Choose complex representatives E_i, zero in all degrees below N, and isomorphisms Q(E_i)≅K_i. Form the filtered diagram S of finite partial sums of E_i. Its objects remain zero below N; evaluation in each degree preserves their finite coproduct cocones.

For any output degree q, apply ordinary qcqs continuity to S. Because S is strictly zero below N, the good-truncation cocone in the continuity theorem is a colimit cocone: its truncation maps are isomorphisms. Invertibility of that theorem’s canonical comparison makes its image under Q followed by Rf_* and H^q a colimit cocone as well.

The finite-partial-sum coproduct universal property needs only preservation of this one filtered diagram. Additivity preserves each finite sum, so the preceding colimit cocone gives preservation of the coproduct E_i under H^q Rf_* Q. This universal-property proof includes the empty family.

Exact coproducts in the module Grothendieck category imply that derived homology preserves coproducts. Factor the coproduct comparison for H^q Rf_* Q as the homology coproduct comparison followed by H^q of the Rf_* Q comparison. The first factor and the composite are invertible, hence the latter is invertible. Homology detects derived isomorphisms, proving that Rf_* Q preserves this coproduct. Since Q sends the termwise coproduct cocone to a derived coproduct cocone, Rf_* preserves the coproduct of Q(E_i). Transport along the representative isomorphisms.

theorem condensed_boundedBelow_preservesCoproduct
    (I : Type (u + 1)) (N : ℤ)
    (K : I → DerivedCategory
      (Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1}) (condensedRingObj Λ X)))
    (hN : ∀ i, (K i).IsGE N) :
    PreservesColimit (Discrete.functor K) R((f)_*⟦Λ⟧)
